items.title: Elephant
facts: Elephants are the largest living land animals on Earth and have super long trunks!
An elephant uses its versatile trunk to drink water, pick up food, and even say hello to friends.

items.title: Lion
facts: Male lions have large, magnificent manes of hair that protect their necks.
A lion's mighty roar can be heard from up to 8 kilometers (5 miles) away!

items.title: Tiger
facts: Every tiger has a completely unique pattern of black stripes, just like human fingerprints!
Unlike many house cats, tigers love water and are wonderful swimmers who cool off in lakes.

items.title: Dog
facts: Dogs communicate their feelings with their tails; a happy wag often means they are joyful!
A dog's sense of smell is up to 100,000 times stronger than a human's sense of smell.

items.title: Cat
facts: Cats make a gentle vibrating sound called a purr when they feel safe, calm, and happy.
Cats use their flexible whiskers to feel the world around them and check if spaces are wide enough.

items.title: Meet the Animals: Wild and Domestic Friends
facts: Animal Kingdom Introduction

items.title: Apple
facts: Apples are sweet, crunchy fruits that grow on trees in orchards and are full of healthy vitamins.

items.title: Banana
facts: Bananas grow in sunny warm places and give our bodies great energy to run and play.

items.title: Mango
facts: The mango is known as the King of Fruits! It is wonderfully sweet, juicy, and delicious.

items.title: Bus
facts: Buses carry many passengers together safely through town, to school, and across cities.

items.title: Car
facts: Cars help families travel together comfortably on roads and highways.

items.title: Cow
facts: Cows are gentle farm animals that give us fresh, nutritious milk every day!
Cows love chewing grass for hours and enjoy resting in sunny green meadows.

items.title: Buffalo
facts: Water buffaloes love cooling off in shallow ponds and rivers on warm days!
They have strong curved horns and help farmers plow fields.

items.title: Goat
facts: Goats are nimble climbers with great balance and love hopping on rocks!
Baby goats are called 'kids' and love jumping and playing together.

items.title: Sheep
facts: Sheep grow thick, soft, curly wool coats that keep us warm in winter sweaters!
Sheep love staying together in friendly groups called flocks.

items.title: Horse
facts: Horses can run very fast and have strong legs with hard hooves!
Horses can sleep both lying down and standing up by locking their leg joints.

items.title: Donkey
facts: Donkeys have large ears that help them hear sounds from far away and stay cool!
They are very patient, sure-footed helpers for farmers.

items.title: Pig
facts: Pigs are among the smartest farm animals and use their flat snouts to sniff out food!
Pigs roll in cool mud to protect their skin from the hot sun.

items.title: Rabbit
facts: Rabbits have long ears to listen carefully and powerful back legs for hopping!
When rabbits are super happy, they jump and twist in the air in a move called a 'binky'.

items.title: Camel
facts: Camels are called the 'Ships of the Desert' and store energy-rich fat in their humps!
Camels have long eyelashes and special nostrils that keep blowing desert sand out.

items.title: Shapes Around Us

items.title: Orange
facts: Oranges are juicy citrus fruits packed with Vitamin C to keep us healthy and strong.

items.title: Grapes
facts: Grapes grow in bunches on vines and are bite-sized sweet treats!

items.title: Watermelon
facts: Watermelons have a green striped rind and sweet, refreshing red fruit inside!

items.title: Pineapple
facts: Pineapples wear a spiky green crown of leaves and are sweet and tangy inside.

items.title: Strawberry
facts: Strawberries are heart-shaped red berries with tiny seeds on the outside!

items.title: Guava
facts: Guavas are fragrant tropical fruits that are crunchy and full of vitamins.

items.title: Papaya
facts: Ripe papayas have soft, sweet orange flesh that is great for tummy health.

items.title: Pomegranate
facts: Inside a pomegranate are hundreds of shiny red jewel-like seeds called arils!

items.title: Coconut
facts: Coconuts grow high on palm trees and hold refreshing coconut water and white meat inside.

items.title: Giraffe
facts: Giraffes are the tallest animals on Earth—their necks can reach high treetop leaves!
A giraffe's tongue is super long (up to 45 cm) and purplish-blue to protect it from sunburn.

items.title: Vegetables and Healthy Food
facts: Vegetables and Healthy Food

items.title: Carrot
facts: Carrots are crunchy orange root vegetables rich in Vitamin A that help our eyes see clearly!

items.title: Peacock
facts: The Indian Peacock is famous for its shimmering blue neck and fan of colorful eye-spotted feathers!
Peacocks love dancing by spreading their grand tail feathers when the monsoon rain clouds arrive.

items.title: Parrot
facts: Parrots have bright green feathers and strong curved red beaks for cracking nuts!
Parrots are super clever birds that can learn to mimic human words and sounds.

items.title: Crow
facts: Crows are glossy black birds and are among the most intelligent problem-solvers in nature!
Remember the story of the thirsty crow who dropped pebbles into a pitcher to raise the water?

items.title: Sparrow
facts: House sparrows are tiny, cheerful brown-and-gray birds that hop quickly on two feet!
Sparrows build cozy cup-shaped nests out of dry grass and soft feathers.

items.title: Pigeon
facts: Pigeons have a remarkable sense of direction and can find their way home from hundreds of miles away!
When pigeons walk, they bob their heads gently to keep their vision steady.

items.title: Eagle
facts: Eagles have huge wingspans that let them glide high above the clouds on warm air currents!
An eagle's eyesight is up to 8 times sharper than a human's eyesight.

items.title: Owl
facts: Owls are nocturnal birds that stay awake at night and have big round eyes to see in the dark!
Owls can turn their heads almost all the way around (up to 270 degrees) without moving their shoulders!

items.title: Duck
facts: Ducks have webbed feet that work like paddles to help them swim smoothly across ponds!
Duck feathers have a natural waterproof coating so their feathers stay dry even when diving.

items.title: Hen
facts: Hens are caring mother birds on the farm that lay nutritious eggs and keep their chicks warm under their wings!
Hens scratch the soil with their feet to find tasty seeds.

items.title: Rooster
facts: The rooster has a bright red comb on top of its head and wakes up the farm at sunrise!
Roosters have shiny, colorful tail feathers and stand on high fences to sing in the morning.

items.title: Penguin
facts: Penguins are birds that cannot fly in the air, but they 'fly' underwater using their flippers as champion swimmers!
Their black-and-white feathers look just like a fancy tuxedo suit.

items.title: Flamingo
facts: Flamingos get their gorgeous pink feather color from the beta-carotene in the tiny shrimp and algae they eat!
Flamingos love standing comfortably on just one long leg in shallow water.

items.title: Ostrich
facts: The ostrich is the largest and heaviest bird in the world and lays the biggest eggs of any bird!
Even though ostriches cannot fly, their long legs let them run faster than a horse.

items.title: Train
facts: Trains roll smoothly on steel railway tracks and carry passengers and goods across long distances!

items.title: Aeroplane
facts: Aeroplanes have big wings and jet engines to fly high above the clouds across countries and oceans!

items.title: Helicopter
facts: Helicopters have spinning rotor blades on top that let them hover in one spot and take off straight up!

items.title: Bicycle
facts: A bicycle has two wheels and pedals that we push with our feet for fun, healthy exercise!

items.title: Motorcycle
facts: A motorcycle is a two-wheeled motor vehicle—riders always wear a strong safety helmet!

items.title: Tractor
facts: Tractors have huge, deep-treaded back wheels to help farmers plow soil and pull farm trailers.

items.title: Truck
facts: Trucks are strong cargo vehicles that carry food, building materials, and supplies to stores.

items.title: Boat
facts: Boats float gently on lakes and rivers using oars, sails, or small motors.

items.title: Ship
facts: Giant ships sail across deep oceans carrying travelers and containers around the world.

items.title: Ambulance
facts: An ambulance has flashing lights and a siren to carry paramedics and help sick people get to the hospital fast.

items.title: Fire Engine
facts: A bright red fire engine carries brave firefighters, long ladders, and water hoses to put out fires!

items.title: Dolphin
facts: Dolphins are friendly, intelligent marine mammals that breathe air through a blowhole on top of their head!
Dolphins talk to each other under the sea using clicks and whistles and love leaping over waves.

items.title: Whale
facts: The Blue Whale is the largest animal ever to live on Earth—even bigger than the biggest dinosaurs!
Whales sing deep, gentle underwater songs that travel for miles through the ocean.

items.title: Shark
facts: Sharks have skeletons made of flexible cartilage instead of hard bone, helping them swim swiftly!
A shark's triangular dorsal fin glides through the water to keep it balanced.

items.title: Octopus
facts: An octopus has eight flexible arms lined with little suction cups and three hearts!
Octopuses are masters of camouflage and can change their skin color in the blink of an eye.

items.title: Sea Turtle
facts: Sea turtles have a hard protective shell and flipper-like legs that let them glide gracefully through the ocean!
Mother sea turtles return to the exact same sandy beach where they were born to lay their eggs.

items.title: Crab
facts: Crabs have ten legs—their front two legs have strong pincers called claws!
Because of the way their leg joints bend, crabs love walking sideways across the sandy beach.

items.title: Jellyfish
facts: Jellyfish have umbrella-shaped bells that pulse gently to float through the water—and they are 95% water!
Jellyfish have drifted through Earth's oceans for hundreds of millions of years.

items.title: Seahorse
facts: A seahorse is a tiny fish with a head shaped like a little horse and a curly tail that holds onto seagrass!
Unlike most animals, it is the father seahorse who carries the babies in a safe pouch until they hatch.

items.title: Starfish
facts: Most starfish have five arms radiating from the center like a star in the sky!
Underneath its arms, a starfish has hundreds of tiny tube feet that help it crawl and hold onto rocks.

items.title: Butterfly
facts: Butterflies start life as tiny caterpillars before transforming inside a chrysalis into winged beauties!
Butterflies taste flower petals with special sensors on their feet.

items.title: Honeybee
facts: Honeybees visit thousands of flowers to collect nectar and make golden sweet honey in hexagonal wax combs!
By carrying pollen from flower to flower, bees help apple, mango, and vegetable plants grow fruit.

items.title: Ant
facts: Ants are super strong—a tiny ant can lift and carry leaves and crumbs up to 20 times its own body weight!
Ants live in big underground cities called colonies and work together as a team.

items.title: Dragonfly
facts: Dragonflies have four shimmering transparent wings that let them hover in mid-air and even fly backward!
Their big compound eyes allow them to see in almost every direction at once.

items.title: Grasshopper
facts: Grasshoppers have long, spring-loaded hind legs that launch them high into the air like little catapults!
They make cheerful summer music by rubbing their back legs against their wings.

items.title: Ladybug
facts: Ladybugs look like shiny red domes with neat black polka dots—and underneath their red shell are hidden wings!
Gardeners love ladybugs because they protect flowers and vegetables from tiny pests.

items.title: Spider
facts: Spiders are arachnids with eight legs, and they spin intricate, silky geometric webs that sparkle with morning dew!
Spider silk is stronger than steel thread of the same thickness.

items.title: Snail
facts: A snail carries its spiral shell house right on its back wherever it goes and can tuck inside when it wants to rest!
Snails glide smoothly on a single muscular foot and have tiny eyes at the tips of their tentacles.

items.title: Frog
facts: Frogs are amphibians that hatch in water as swimming tadpoles and grow legs to hop onto land!
Tree frogs have sticky round pads on their toes to climb smooth green leaves.

items.title: Crocodile
facts: Crocodiles have tough, scaly armor plates along their backs that warm up like solar panels in the sun!
When a crocodile rests on the riverbank with its mouth open, it is actually cooling itself down.

items.title: Snake
facts: Snakes have no legs at all, yet they glide smoothly across the ground and up trees using special belly scales!
Snakes flick their forked tongues in and out to smell the air around them.

items.title: Lizard
facts: Lizards are cold-blooded reptiles that love doing little push-ups on warm sunny rocks in the morning!
Many lizards can safely regrow their tail if it ever gets caught.

items.title: Chameleon
facts: Chameleons can change the color of their skin to match their mood, temperature, and leafy surroundings!
A chameleon's two eyes can look in two completely different directions at the same time.

items.title: Tortoise
facts: A tortoise walks on land with sturdy, elephant-like feet and carries a high, domed protective shell!
Tortoises walk slowly and peacefully, and they can live for more than 100 years!

items.title: Ball
facts: A round, bouncy play ball is great for kicking, catching, and rolling with friends outdoors!

items.title: Book
facts: Books are filled with stories, pictures, and knowledge that take our imagination on wonderful adventures!

items.title: Pencil
facts: We hold a pencil to write letters, numbers, and draw creative pictures on paper.

items.title: Chair
facts: A sturdy chair has four legs and a backrest so we can sit comfortably while reading or eating.

items.title: Table
facts: A table has a flat top where families gather to eat meals, study, and build puzzles.

items.title: Clock
facts: A clock has numbers from 1 to 12 and moving hands that tell us the time of day!

items.title: Umbrella
facts: An umbrella opens like a canopy overhead to keep us dry in the rain and shaded from hot sun.

items.title: Shoes
facts: We wear comfortable shoes on our feet to protect them when walking, running, and playing outside.

items.title: Bag
facts: A school backpack bag has shoulder straps to carry our books, pencils, and lunchbox neatly.

items.title: Bottle
facts: A reusable water bottle keeps clean drinking water ready so we stay hydrated all day!

items.title: Cup
facts: A cup has a curved handle so we can hold it safely to drink warm milk or water.

items.title: Spoon
facts: We use a clean spoon to scoop and eat soup, rice, yogurt, and cereal.

items.title: Toothbrush
facts: A toothbrush has soft bristles that clean our teeth every morning and night for a bright smile!

items.title: Bed
facts: A cozy bed has a soft mattress, pillow, and blanket where we sleep and recharge every night.

items.title: Rainbow
facts: A rainbow appears in the sky when sunlight shines through raindrops, showing seven glowing colors!

items.title: Sun
facts: The Sun is a bright star at the center of our solar system that gives Earth warm daylight and helps plants grow!

items.title: Moon
facts: The Moon shines softly in the night sky and changes shape from a thin crescent to a bright full circle!

items.title: Stars
facts: Stars are distant suns twinkling across the night sky in beautiful patterns called constellations.

items.title: Cloud
facts: Clouds float in the sky and are made of tiny water droplets that bring refreshing rain to the Earth.

items.title: Tree
facts: Trees have deep roots, a sturdy trunk, and green leaves that make fresh oxygen for us to breathe!

items.title: Flower
facts: Flowers bloom with colorful petals and sweet fragrance, inviting bees and butterflies to visit.

items.title: Mountain
facts: Mountains are giant landforms that rise high into the sky, often crowned with white snow at the peak!

items.title: River
facts: A river is a flowing ribbon of fresh water that travels from mountains down through valleys to the sea.

items.title: Waterfall
facts: A waterfall happens where a river tumbles over a high rocky cliff into a misty pool below!

items.title: Ocean
facts: The ocean is a vast body of salty water that covers most of our planet and is home to whales, dolphins, and coral reefs!
